assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Television Episodes 4-13 in located states: the subway battle and his reaction to the 'accident' cover (E04); the killing of a young Lycoris (E05); the first fight with Chisato and his revised regard for Robota (E06); recognition of Chisato as the child of the old tower (E07); the private visit and the old-tower recollection (E08); the meeting with Yoshimatsu and the political questioning of Kusunoki (E09-E10); the public gun broadcast, the constraint on Chisato through Yoshimatsu and the old-tower fight (E10-E11); capture by Alpha Four and return (E12, 02:57 and 21:54-22:41); the rematch, his statement that his work is finished, and the bandaged street scene (E13). The armed attack at the old radio tower ten years earlier is his remembered history and belongs to him at every state. From E12 02:57 he is in custody and has no witnessed knowledge of Chisato's intervention to save Takina or of the heart's provenance. Nothing after his E13 street scene; anthology stories are outside scope.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait gives an organizing account: distrust of concealed authority that arranges the world for a public kept ignorant (the 'lie' of sanitized peace, E04; the questions to Kusunoki about law and public judgment, E10 C0169-0218); a demand that deaths and acts be witnessed rather than absorbed into a word ('accident', E04); remembered fear of the child at the old tower turned into a search for the one opponent who balances him (E07-E08, E13); and loyalty to his comrades that also serves as leverage (the twenty-six dead used to set Robota a three-day deadline, E06). It predicts his overreach as well as his principles: he reads the part of Chisato's resistance that resembles his own as kinship and rides past the part that forbids partnership (E11), turns her account of what she values into a claim to be her final client (E13), and asks a frightened public to judge with their own eyes after manufacturing what they see (E10-E11). Not B: the portrait states that his principle of siding with the weak is an untested conditional whose referent shifts (a group whose dead are erased, an institution that may lose, an opponent denied a contest), that the vulnerable people he harms or pressures do not win his aid, and, in its own conditional example, that it cannot say whether he would protect a person's wish for anonymity, accept an outcome or simply pursue another opponent ('That is the unresolved part of the man'). Which motive decides where the political project, the personal contest and his comrades' interests diverge is not established, which is insufficiency rather than productive uncertainty. Not D: the account carries located conditions (audience size, peer status, concealed authority, the opponent's condition) that support narrow prediction.

Located shifts in his relation to Chisato: an opponent he taunts and identifies by her pendant (E06), recognition of the old-tower child (E07), a private visit with film talk and a drink (E08), an attempt to recruit her by constraining her through Yoshimatsu (E10-E11), and a rematch on his terms after his work is declared finished (E13). His regard for Robota moves from dismissal to praise and 'ours' (E04-E07, E09-E10). Not B: his core stance does not change across the span, and the decade since the old tower is known only from one recollection; steps between custody and return are uncertain (E12). Not D: the states are cut-located and ordered.

Located address habits only: the easy plural 'we' that Chisato makes him account for (E08), correcting 'your plan' to 'ours' and later 'my hacker' (E07, E13), 俺の仲間 for his comrades against 'pawns' (E06), the epithet 黒いほう for Takina (E10, E13), a school-trip joke that deflates the Lycoris' rank (E10), contemptuous public address (E10-E11), and 'Don't die yet' with the diagnosis 'a bad sound' (E13). Not C: the portrait gives no register rules (first-person forms, endings, politeness by listener), no continuous audiovisual performance was verified, and the discovery row does not claim speech. Not E: several individuated habits recur across episodes.

A few located ordinary preferences inside confrontations: enthusiasm for Die Hard and its partnership plot (E08 C0281-0287), declining bitter coffee and asking for something else (E08), finding Chisato's drink too sweet (E13), and steadying a frightened stranger while returning a handgun (E13). Anthology scenes (vegetables advice, a parfait, a rental-shop visit) are creator-local and outside the continuity. Not C: there is no routine, home, food or leisure beyond these moments, and his age, family and domestic life are undisclosed. Not E: the preferences are specific and located across two episodes.

The portrait differentiates his responses by relationship with a stated mechanism for each: Robota (bullied and dismissed, then praised specifically when he delivers, then included as 'ours' and 'my hacker' while Majima keeps deciding his place, E04-E13); Chisato (the one person he says frightened him, a peer whose refusal makes her worth having, a host with whom ordinary talk is possible, and a person he coerces, E06-E13); Kusunoki (mocking the institution's dignity, then serious questions about legitimacy, E10); Yoshimatsu (objection to being reminded of a favor, disgust at self-sacrifice to the ideal, use of his position against Chisato, E09-E11); his comrades (counted dead, livelihood cited as a reason for paid work, E06, E10); Takina (mutual disinterest, later a concession that she is the better shot, E10, E13); and the public (contempt and a lesson imposed on bystanders, E10-E11). Not A: most relations rest on a few scenes; his followers' closeness to him after the audience disperses is uncertain, and the Takina relation is two exchanges. Not C: the differences are located and their conditions are named (competence delivered, peer status, concealed authority, debt).

Access is through his own speech and one remembered scene: saying alone that he has once again been the one left (E04), the old-tower recollection that renders the child as a monster from his fear (E08), his statement of disgust at Yoshimatsu's creed (E10), and his admission that Chisato is the only one who has frightened him (E13). Not C: there is no inner monologue, the portrait reaches no settled account of what he feels for Chisato beyond declarations of fear, affinity and interest, and his formative history is undisclosed. Not E: several self-disclosures are located across episodes.

His conflict modes are varied and located with conditions: deadline threats that use his comrades' deaths (E06); taunts in combat over nonlethal ammunition (E06); gun-point visits with conversational ease that he ends on his own terms when a third party arrives (E08); using Yoshimatsu's safety to dictate Chisato's movements (E11); orientation by hearing that lets him fight in the dark (E08, E11); after defeat, a demand for a rematch without her partner on terms he calls fair (E13); a rest granted to an unwell opponent while the tower timer keeps running (E13). Not A: his response to a defeat is seen once, his tactical planning is mostly Robota's, and the clinical basis of his hearing is unexplained. Not C: the portrait separates what he concedes (time, a pause, a taste of the drink) from what he never concedes (the threat, the timer, her partner's exclusion).

He states positions and argues them: whether Direct Attack exists under law, how the public would judge the arrangements if they knew, that an institution should not put its thumb on the scales either way, that peace must be won and not merely felt, and that he always sides with the weak (E10 C0169-0218; E13 C0123-0140). The portrait tests these against his acts: the killed young Lycoris (E05), the bystanders handed guns (E10-E11), Robota under deadline, and the unaudited three thousand disappearances offered as insinuation (E10). Not B: he is not shown weighing competing goods; the 'weak' principle is untested and inconsistently applied, and the portrait abstains on what he would do when publicity and a weaker person's wishes conflict. Not D: the stated principles are located and carry counterevidence.

A few located instances: treating Lycoris as a school trip with a chaperone (E10), laughing at Chisato's denial that she remembers him (E08) and the shared pleasure of the Die Hard conversation (E08). Not C: the instances are few and their function (deflating official authority) is stated once. Not E: the style is individuated and recurs.

One dedicated, cut- and timecode-located portrait covers his appearances in Episodes 4-13 with links to the readings and the TV reconciliation, and separates TV evidence from creator-local anthology readings. Not B: it is an essayistic portrait rather than an enumeration; it states that no continuous audiovisual performance was verified, speech is not claimed, and the ledgers and readings behind it are not on the row. Not D: every major appearance is located.

Affirmative bounds are located: the twenty-six dead are his reported count and cannot be allocated to the fight shown (E06); the three thousand disappearances are unaudited insinuation (E10); reading his pursuit as an imitation of Die Hard turns a resonance into an undeclared motive (E08); he has no basis to expect Chisato to remember him, and she denies it (E08); a film preference and quiet exchange do not certify alliance; the evidence for romance is much thinner than for fear, affinity and interest; the 'weak' principle does not win aid for the vulnerable people he harmed or pressured (E13); he has no witnessed knowledge of events after his capture (E12); the E13 comparison concerns two people, not a weapon's contents (verifier Q19); and anthology scenes belong to their contributors. Not A: no forecast about him is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

States are placed by episode, cut and timecode, with the old-tower attack ten years earlier and custody from E12 02:57. Not B: there is no story calendar, the route from custody to the E12 return is uncertain, and his age is undisclosed. Not D: the sequence and the two tower encounters are precisely located.

scenario_readiness.note: The portrait gives address habits but no register rules, no continuous performance was verified, and the discovery row does not claim speech; generated lines would be constrained only by content, not by a source-supported voice.

conditions: An institutional representative defends concealed authority: predict a joke that deflates rank, then serious questions about legality and how the public would judge, and the claim that no institution should put its thumb on the scales (E10).

A subordinate delivers useful work: predict specific praise, a revised opinion stated aloud and inclusive 'ours', while he keeps deciding the subordinate's place; a failure or a frightened excuse draws a deadline backed by his comrades' losses (E04-E07).
A peer-level opponent he respects is unwell during a contest: predict a pause and 'don't die yet', with no concession on the threat or deadline he has set (E13).

A private encounter with a respected adversary in which a shared interest appears: predict real engagement and ordinary requests (a drink, a film question) while the danger he brought stays in place and he leaves on his own terms when a third party arrives (E08).
After a defeat by two people: predict a demand for a rematch against the one he regards as his counterpart, on terms he calls fair (E13).

Include his mistakes: claiming kinship from a resemblance of resistance, casting another person's values as a reason to serve him, and imposing on bystanders the conditions of the lesson he wants taught.
Exclude whether he would protect a person's wish for anonymity, accept an outcome he dislikes, or help a weaker party in practice; his formative history; romance; anything after E13.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Television Episodes 4-13: before E07 he does not connect Chisato with the old-tower child; from E07 he does; from E12 02:57 he is in custody without witnessed knowledge of later events until his return at the end of E12; after E13 nothing is modeled. The old-tower attack ten years earlier is remembered history at every state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: The sampled relations: Robota as subordinate, Chisato as feared and respected opponent, Kusunoki and Yoshimatsu as representatives of concealed authority, his comrades, and the Tokyo public as audience. Any other interlocutor is a separate, lower-confidence transfer limited to the nearest sampled relation.
setting_constraints: Tokyo of the television series, with Direct Attack, the Lycoris and the Alan Institute as the series presents them.
No anthology scene, no clinical account of his hearing, no event after E13 and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation is supported where the portrait gives a located precedent; the choices that would discriminate among his motives are excluded.
Ordinary sociability appears only inside confrontations he controls (a film conversation, a drink request, a taste of a sweet drink); there is no routine or life outside the conflict to model.

conditions: Limited to argument with a representative of concealed authority about legitimacy, law and public knowledge, using his stated positions (E10).
His 'side with the weak' claim may be stated, with the inconsistency the portrait records; no prediction that he aids a particular vulnerable person.
No new ethical choice under conflicting goods is predicted.
scenario_readiness.note: His stated principles are located and argued, but their application is inconsistent, so only argument about legitimacy is supported, not his choices.
The portrait states that the evidence for romance is much thinner than his declarations of fear, affinity and personal interest in Chisato, who repeatedly contests his claim to speak for them both.

conditions: Leading his group: predict that he cites his comrades' livelihood when asked about money, separates the commissioned job from what he pursues for his own reasons, counts his dead and uses them as leverage (E06, E10).
Directing a technical specialist: predict that he asks for the objective, cuts explanations short, and praises or threatens by results (E04-E09).
Excluded: tactical planning detail, the clients' commission beyond Kusunoki's account, and his earlier international career.
scenario_readiness.note: His conduct as leader of paid fighters is located in several scenes; operational planning is mostly Robota's and the international career is reported by Kusunoki.

known_limits.statement: The portrait gives address habits but no register analysis; no continuous audiovisual performance was independently verified, and the discovery row does not claim speech.

The portrait leaves open which motive decides when his political aim, his personal contest and other people's wishes diverge; its own conditional example cannot say whether he would protect anonymity, accept an outcome or seek another opponent.

His claim always to side with the weak is an untested conditional offered to an adversary; its referent shifts, and the young Lycoris he killed, the frightened stranger and Robota under deadline did not win his aid.
His age, early family life, intimate history, domestic life and the basis of his hearing are undisclosed or unexplained in the TV evidence.

From E12 02:57 he is in custody and has no witnessed knowledge of Chisato's intervention to save Takina or of the heart's provenance; Chisato tells him she does not know him from the old-tower encounter, so he has no confirmation that she remembers it.
Anthology scenes (followers' superstition, the rental shop, a café visit, advice to Robota) belong to their named contributors, are outside the television continuity, and are not used for prediction.
There is no evidence of his conduct after the E13 street scene, or of whether anyone acts on his prediction of Direct Attack's downfall.
